elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The consent-free Customer carve-out covers only a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets; it does not cover assignment to an Affiliate generally.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Clause 22.4(a) states that M&I's consent is not required for assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Clause 22.4(b) permits M&I to assign freely to a successor in connection with a merger or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock, or securities.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general consent requirement states that the other party's prior written consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, which applies to M&I assignments outside clause 22.4(b).

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no prohibition on assignment by M&I to a Customer competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: The change-of-control provision requires M&I to continue providing Services, subject to stated scope and volume limitations, and grants no termination right.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Clause 22.4(a) permits Customer assignment to a successor in specified transactions, and clause 22.4(b) permits M&I assignment to a successor in specified transactions.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The final sentence requires the assigning party to give the other party written notice of any assignment under clause (a) or (b).
The opening sentence prohibits assignment by either party without the other party's prior written consent, except for the successor-assignment carve-outs in clauses (a) and (b).

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence provides that the required consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.
